subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should own the public web-tool egress boundary: a scoped `web_fetch` hostname policy, a managed-proxy policy, or a broader cross-tool domain policy covering search/fetch/browser/provider paths?
rationale: This is a new operator-trusted security/config surface, and the related open PRs propose different boundaries that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review the narrow hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause in-process web_fetch domain config and route app-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require cross-tool design first
options.body: Hold implementation until fetch, search, browser, redirects, caches, provider fallback, and plugin HTTP are covered by one security contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review the narrow hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across SSRF helpers, guarded fetch, and web_fetch runtime behavior.
